title: Reconcile API & Webhook Contract for Idempotent Optimize Applies and Rollbacks
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Design and implement a reconciler API and webhook contract that enables Optimize automation to safely apply batching/caching recommendations and trigger rollbacks. The goal is an end-to-end idempotent flow for server-side applies, deterministic rollbacks, and robust webhook delivery semantics so customers and downstream systems can rely on exactly-once effects or safe retries.
acceptance_criteria: A POST /optimize/v1/reconciles endpoint exists that accepts a recommendation bundle and returns a stable operation_id and HTTP 202 for async processing
Server guarantees idempotent apply semantics when clients retry with the same Idempotency-Key header: repeated requests with identical payload+key must not apply changes more than once
Every reconcile operation produces a deterministic plan-version and a human-readable summary included in responses and webhooks
Webhook deliveries include a delivery_id and original idempotency key; receivers can acknowledge receips via /webhooks/ack to suppress retries
Failed applies automatically create a rollback operation with a link to the user-visible rollback operation_id; rollbacks are idempotent as well
SDK exposes helper primitives to synthesize and persist idempotency keys and to perform safe retries with exponential backoff
Metrics are emitted for apply_success_rate, apply_duplicate_rate, webhook_delivery_attempts, webhook_ack_latency, and rollback_duration
E2E tests cover network failures, duplicated requests, partial failures during multi-step applies, and webhook consumer slow/failed ACKs
spec: API contract summary:

- POST /optimize/v1/reconciles: Accepts payload {recommendations: [...], target: {project_id, route}, client_metadata} and optional Idempotency-Key header. Returns 202 + {operation_id, plan_version, status_url}
- GET /optimize/v1/reconciles/{operation_id}: Returns current state, events, and applied_patch_id if complete
- POST /optimize/v1/reconciles/{operation_id}/rollback: Triggers a rollback; accepts Idempotency-Key and returns rollback_operation_id
- POST /optimize/v1/webhooks/ack: Webhook consumers call this to confirm processing; accepts delivery_id and consumer_id
Idempotency rules:

- Server uses a composite idempotency key derived from Idempotency-Key header + SHA256(payload) + target route. If same composite key is seen, server returns the original operation_id and current status instead of creating a new operation

- For long-running applies, apply is broken into ordered stages: validate -> plan -> apply-prechecks -> apply-changes -> verify. If a retry arrives in middle, stages detect previously completed checkpoints using operation state and are no-ops for replayed stages
Webhook semantics:
- Webhook envelope includes: delivery_id, operation_id, plan_version, event_type (applied, failed, rollback_started, rollback_completed), timestamp, idempotency_key

- Delivery guarantees are at-least-once; the platform will retry webhook deliveries with exponential backoff until ACK or TTL (72h). To reduce duplicate processing, consumers should dedupe using delivery_id or idempotency_key
- Consumers can call POST /webhooks/ack to confirm receipt; ack immediately halts further retries for that delivery_id
Rollback semantics:

- Any apply failure that crosses the transactional safety threshold (configurable) schedules a rollback operation that attempts to revert only the changes recorded in apply-change log entries. Rollback operations have the same idempotency guarantees as applies
SDK primitives:

- reconcileClient.apply(recommendations, opts): returns {operation_id, status_url}. opts includes clientProvidedKey (string) or sdkAutoKey (boolean). The SDK persists keys for 72h by default and performs safe retries transparently
- reconcileClient.watch(operation_id, onUpdate): helper to subscribe to server-sent events or polling with backoff, exposes final outcome and failure reason
Observability and audit:
- Every reconcile operation writes an audit entry with operator, plan_version, diff, and KMS-encrypted payload reference (if sensitive). Logs include idempotency_key and delivery history for webhooks
Security:

- All endpoints require customer API key with permission scope 'optimize:reconcile' or equivalent. Webhook ack endpoint requires the webhook consumer secret header for authenticity. Security team to review TLS, signature, and replay protections
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary): Implement server-side idempotency storage and POST /reconciles; enable for 5% of internal Optimize traffic behind feature flag
Phase 2 (SDK): Ship SDK primitives in beta release to internal teams and one pilot customer; collect metrics and consumer feedback
Phase 3 (webhooks): Turn on webhook delivery with ack endpoint and DLQ; enable retries and monitor duplicate rates
Phase 4 (GA): Open to all customers, surface config in Console under Optimize automation with toggle and audit logs
test_plan: Unit tests for idempotency store semantics and composite key generation
Integration tests simulating duplicate requests (same key, different payload) and ensuring server returns original operation and does not double-apply
Chaos tests that inject transient network failures between apply stages and verify rollback scheduling and successful compensation
Webhook consumer tests: unresponsive consumer, duplicate delivery, late ack; verify platform retry behavior and DLQ placement
SDK e2e tests that persist keys locally then simulate client crash and resume to verify safe retry behavior
notes: Design trade-offs: Strong idempotency requires durable storage for keys which increases read/write load; compromise: TTL 7 days for idempotency entries and provisioned RCU for heavy traffic targets
Decision: Use composite key (Idempotency-Key + payload hash + target) instead of payload-only to avoid accidental merges across routes
We considered a two-phase commit across downstream subsystems but rejected for complexity and latency; chosen approach is staged apply with checkpointed state and compensating rollback steps
Risk: Webhook consumers that are not idempotent will observe duplicates; mitigation: clearly documented webhook envelope and provide SDK consumer helpers that perform dedupe using delivery_id
Telemetry: expose dashboard in Console for 'Optimize Reconcile' showing inflight operations, duplicate rate, average apply duration, and rollback frequency
